issues.description: Objective IDs ('lo-tc-01', 'lo-tc-02') are used as prerequisite references - three occurrences. The provenance notes describe these as a model-proposed prerequisite chain, so the intent is a sequencing statement, but the values do not resolve to prerequisite entities.
Three further occurrences of objective IDs in prerequisite_refs.

Six occurrences mixing objective IDs ('lo-tc-01', 'lo-tc-02') and lesson IDs ('les-tc-01-01', 'les-tc-02-01', 'les-tc-03-01') into a prerequisite reference field. Three distinct entity types now share one field.
All three modules declare lesson_ids: []. Six lessons carry valid module_id back-references, so the outline cannot be traversed downward to its lessons even though the reverse lookup succeeds.

All three are flagged is_summative=true, yet all three are attached to lessons via formative_assessment_ids (les-tc-01-02, les-tc-02-02, les-tc-03-02). The artifact declares no formative assessment and simultaneously uses every summative as one.

The brief's desired performance is a single integrated act - structure an explanation and adapt terminology for a non-specialist audience. Three assessments each cover one objective; none requires both structuring and terminology adaptation in one artifact, so the terminal capability is never assessed as a whole.

Each is status=candidate and simultaneously carries teaching_objective_id pointing at an objective in this course. Presented as candidates rather than confirmed, so provenance is handled correctly, but the dual role (entry gate and teaching target) is left unresolved with no stated intake policy.

technical_review.notes: Objective coverage is complete: each of the three objectives has a module, two lessons and a dedicated assessment. The defects are concentrated in two fields. prerequisite_refs is overloaded across objectives, modules and lessons with objective and lesson IDs alongside genuine prerequisite IDs (twelve occurrences), and modules[].lesson_ids is empty throughout. Rubric dimension IDs are defined and referenced correctly in every mastery rule. No validator output was included in the packet, so `validator_appears_correct` is null on every issue; the findings below are the reviewer's own reference walk over the artifact, not a confirmation or contradiction of a quality gate.

special_question.notes: Answered independently of the empty lesson_ids, the overloaded prerequisite_refs and the is_summative flags. On instruction alone this is the strongest of the two technical-communication packets. Objectives are written with unusual care about evaluability - lo-tc-02 requires that structure be 'identifiable without requiring domain expertise to evaluate' and lo-tc-03 requires the revision be 'assessable without access to the original specialist source', which are rater-facing design decisions, not just learner-facing criteria. Each module runs model-then-produce (worked example or scenario, then independent practice) with the majority of minutes on production: 12 of 20 in mod-tc-02, 17 of 25 in mod-tc-03. The rubrics name where human judgement is irreducible rather than pretending it can be automated. Two design reservations sit under this: the three sub-capabilities are never recombined into the single integrated performance the brief asks for, and because every assessment doubles as the lesson's own practice output, there is no unscaffolded observation anywhere in the design.

rubric_scores.rationale: Each objective states its givens, the performance and criteria that a rater can apply without ambiguity, including explicit evaluability constraints - 'structure is identifiable without requiring domain expertise to evaluate', 'revised text is assessable without access to the original specialist source'. lo-tc-03 also names who can judge accuracy ('as judged by a domain-informed evaluator'). The assumption notes flag that 'logical sequence' is undefined in the brief and must be validated, which is precisely the caveat a reviewer needs.

One assessment per objective with evidence statements that track the success criteria line by line - ev-tc-03-a/b/c against lo-tc-03's three criteria, in order. Nothing assessed is unclaimed and nothing claimed is unassessed at the objective level. Held at 4 because the brief's desired performance is the combined act and no assessment requires structuring and terminology adaptation in the same artifact.

Learner-produced written artifacts at each stage, three-level rubrics with genuinely discriminating descriptors (the middle level of rd-tc-03-2 - 'no clear inaccuracies but meaning is distorted or oversimplified to the point of misleading' - captures the exact failure mode of plain-language rewriting), and an explicit statement that factual accuracy needs a domain-informed human evaluator. Two deductions: each artifact is produced inside the lesson that taught it, so none is unscaffolded evidence; and every mastery rule requires the top level on every dimension, which will misclassify solid work.

analyze for audience characterisation, apply for structuring and for terminology adaptation, with assessment cognitive_process matching each. Lesson patterns escalate correctly in every module - explanation then guided practice, worked example then independent practice, scenario then independent practice - and the time split favours production, which is what apply-level objectives require.

Five candidates, all correctly qualified, each with a rationale naming the objective or assessment that requires it, a full dependency chain, and teaching_objective_id used to mark which could be taught if absent. That last is thoughtful design. Loses a point on minimality and coherence: pre-tc-01 (adult reading literacy) and pre-tc-04 (write coherent multi-sentence English) are near-universal gates that no intake process would act on, and three items are simultaneously entry conditions and teaching targets with no stated rule for what happens when a learner lacks them.

Audience -> structure -> terminology, with each transition justified in the sequencing_rationale by reference to the declared dependency and explicitly labelled as requiring researcher validation. Minutes increase across modules (15, 20, 25) in proportion to the production demand of each objective, which is the right shape.

Every module models the performance and then has the learner produce it, and the produced artifact is exactly what the rubric scores - les-tc-03-01 has learners flag specialist terms and justify why each needs adapting, which is the direct precursor to rd-tc-03-1. The deduction is that preparation and assessment are the same event: the independent practice lesson is where the summative artifact is produced, so there is no separate opportunity to fail safely first.

Moderate. No feedback loop is specified anywhere - the practice lessons produce the graded artifact with no intermediate check, so a learner who misunderstands in les-tc-02-01 has no correction before les-tc-02-02 is scored. lo-tc-01 gets 15 minutes total for an analyze-level objective, and the combined performance the brief wants is never rehearsed.
None. Six lessons, three modules, 60 minutes exactly, every lesson tied to an objective, no content beyond the three objectives and no padded breadth.

Resolve the summative/formative split so at least one observation is unscaffolded, add an integrated task covering the brief's combined performance, and relax the all-dimensions-at-top mastery rules. The objectives, rubrics, sequence and lesson content need no rewriting.

prerequisite_acceptance.notes: pre-tc-02 (a working concept of audience as a variable in communication), pre-tc-03 (distinguishing specialist from non-specialist vocabulary) and pre-tc-05 (understanding logical sequence in expository writing) are the substantive ones: each is genuinely required by a specific objective, each is correctly marked candidate, and each carries a rationale tied to the objective that needs it. They are accepted, but with a required revision - all three carry teaching_objective_id pointing into this course while also being declared entry conditions, and the artifact never states what happens at intake if a learner lacks them. Either the status should say 'candidate, taught if absent' or the dual role should be removed. pre-tc-01 (read at general adult literacy) and pre-tc-04 (produce coherent multi-sentence English) are rejected as prerequisites: both are true of essentially any learner reaching a technical-communication course, neither can be screened or remediated in any meaningful way, and listing them dilutes the three that matter. They belong in audience_notes, not in the prerequisite set.

edit_effort.notes: Estimated: three is_summative flags corrected plus one integrated assessment authored; two prerequisites dropped and three given an explicit intake policy; one module extended or retimed to hold the integrated task; two independent-practice lessons split so a scaffolded attempt precedes the scored one. Objectives, rubrics and sequencing stand as written.

pedagogical_review.overall_notes: The best-written objectives and rubrics of the technical-communication pair, and notable for stating its own limits - that 'logical sequence' is undefined in the brief, that factual accuracy cannot be scored without a domain expert, that the prerequisite chain is a candidate requiring validation. Against that, the artifact labels every assessment summative while using each one as in-lesson practice, so as written it produces no unscaffolded evidence and never assesses the combined performance the brief actually describes.
